newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Freed Ershad vows support for Bangladesh ruler.
newsitem.headline: Freed Ershad vows support for Bangladesh ruler.

text.p: Bangladesh's former president Hossain Mohammad Ershad said his Jatiya Party would support the government of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina until the next general elections in 2001.
"Our support will remain intact for the government through its full term of five years. We believe that supporting a good government means doing good for the people," he said.
Ershad was speaking to reporters on Sunday night after saying prayers at the tombs of two Moslem saints in Sylhet town in the country's tea-growing northeastern district.
It was his first visit outside Dhaka after being released from jail on Thursday.
Ershad said: "We are not giving unconditional support to Hasina. We will certainly criticise her for doing anything bad for the people."
Ershad's party supported Hasina's Awami League in forming a government following a general election last June. He fought the election from jail and was elected a member of parliament.

Begum Khaleda Zia, chief of the main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), alleged that Ershad's release after six years in prison was the result of a "successful conspiracy" between Ershad's party and the Awami League.
Ershad rejected the allegation as an "outburst of (Khaleda's) dismal political prospects."
Ershad walked out of jail a day after he was granted bail by the Supreme Court on the last of a series of corruption charges against him.
Ershad, a retired army general who seized power in a 1982 bloodless coup, had been in jail since he was toppled in a popular uprising in December 1990.
"Every political party wants to run the country. We have long experience in running the country," Ershad said on Sunday.
"God and people willing, we hope to govern again," he said.
"But I don't foresee an early election. I don't think the opposition now has any strong issue at hand to press for that," Ershad added.
